questions.question: Retention
questions.answer: Local memory stays on the user's machine. Cloud: data uploaded in REM Enhanced mode (and Agent Native's default nightly Self Learning upload) stays in the user's own space in Sno's cloud and is not deleted automatically; no retention period or post-account-closure retention is stated.

questions.question: Deletion
questions.answer: Locally, uninstall --purge-state removes state. In Sno's cloud the user can open their own space and delete uploaded memory text, lessons and sessions; nothing there is deleted automatically. Account-level cloud deletion and its timing are not documented.

questions.answer: Consent doc and README describe what leaves the computer.

questions.question: Telemetry default
questions.answer: On by default: uploads to Sno start without an opt-in. In sno-station commit e13d286 (newer than the scoped v2.0.2 tag 44e2d7c) the observability package defaults to metadata-only (usage events, no text); the sno-cli v1.3.5 README (newer than the scoped v1.3.2) says full is the default. Either way usage data leaves the machine by default; the disagreement about which level is kept visible.

questions.question: Telemetry controls
questions.answer: sno station consent off/metadata-only/full, pause/resume.

questions.question: Telemetry off switch location
questions.answer: In the app: the product is CLI-based and its own documented consent command, `sno station consent off`, stops uploads (sno-station commit e13d286 README and consent.ts; sno-cli v1.3.5 README); there is no separate settings screen or first-run consent step.

questions.question: Consent prompt
questions.answer: Onboarding asks how Sno should work and what it uploads.

questions.question: Provider separation
questions.answer: Model provider policies separate from Sno's.

limitations: Default consent stated differently in two first-party docs; hosted processing details (retention period, subprocessors, residency) not documented; cloud uploads are kept until the user deletes them.

claims.answer: The software is free open source; the hosted Sno engine gives a weekly free allowance (a tenth until the computer is linked) then a dollar balance; prices, currency, interval and trial terms are not published in the repositories or site pages checked.
